title: EPA 609 approved refrigerant handling equipment
description: Which refrigerant handling equipment counts as approved under 40 CFR 82.36 for MVAC service: the standard for each refrigerant, older equipment and EPA's list.
summary: Refrigerant recycling equipment must be certified by EPA or by an independent standards testing organization approved by EPA under 82.38 to meet the standard that 82.36(a) sets for its refrigerant and function. Equipment that has not been certified is considered approved if it is substantially identical to certified equipment and was initially purchased before the dates in 82.36(b)(1). EPA maintains a list of approved equipment by manufacturer and model.
intro: This page covers what makes refrigerant handling equipment approved for MVAC and MVAC-like appliance service under 40 CFR 82.36, with the related definitions and prohibitions in 82.32 and 82.34. Each point quotes the rule and links to it.

points.text: No person repairing or servicing MVACs for consideration, and no person repairing or servicing MVAC-like appliances, may perform service involving the refrigerant without properly using equipment approved under 82.36.
points.quote: No person repairing or servicing MVACs for consideration, and no person repairing or servicing MVAC-like appliances, may perform any service involving the refrigerant for such MVAC or MVAC-like appliance: (1) Without properly using equipment approved pursuant to § 82.36;

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.34, Prohibitions and required practices (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Approved refrigerant recycling equipment is equipment certified by EPA (the Administrator) or by an organization approved under 82.38 as meeting a standard in 82.36. It extracts and recycles refrigerant, or extracts it for recycling on-site or reclamation off-site.
points.quote: Approved refrigerant recycling equipment means equipment certified by the Administrator or an organization approved under § 82.38 as meeting either one of the standards in § 82.36. Such equipment extracts and recycles refrigerant or extracts refrigerant for recycling on-site or reclamation off-site.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.32, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Properly using the equipment includes operating it according to the manufacturer's guide to operation and maintenance, and using it only for the controlled substance it is designed for.
points.quote: In addition, this term includes operating the equipment in accordance with the manufacturer's guide to operation and maintenance and using the equipment only for the controlled substance for which the machine is designed.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.32, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Refrigerant handling equipment made or imported for servicing MVACs for consideration cannot be introduced into interstate commerce unless it meets 82.36.
points.quote: Refrigerant handling equipment manufactured or imported for use during the maintenance, service or repair of MVACs for consideration cannot be introduced into interstate commerce unless meeting the requirements of § 82.36.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.34, Prohibitions and required practices (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Anyone opening MVAC-like appliances must have at least one piece of approved recovery or recycling equipment available at their place of business.
points.quote: All persons opening (as that term is defined in § 82.152) MVAC-like appliances must have at least one piece of approved recovery or recycling equipment available at their place of business.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.32, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

topics.name: The standard for each kind of equipment

points.text: Refrigerant recycling equipment must be certified by EPA, or by an independent standards testing organization approved by EPA under 82.38, to meet the applicable standard listed in 82.36(a).
points.quote: Refrigerant recycling equipment must be certified by the Administrator or an independent standards testing organization approved by the Administrator under § 82.38 to meet the following standard:

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.36, Approved refrigerant handling equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: CFC-12, recover and recycle: Appendix A.
points.quote: Equipment that recovers and recycles CFC-12 refrigerant must meet the standards set forth in appendix A of this subpart

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.36, Approved refrigerant handling equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: CFC-12, recover only (no recycling): Appendix B.
points.quote: Equipment that recovers but does not recycle CFC-12 refrigerant must meet the standards set forth in appendix B of this subpart

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.36, Approved refrigerant handling equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: HFC-134a, recover and recycle, or recover, recycle and recharge: Appendix C (based on SAE J2788), effective January 1, 2008.
points.quote: Effective January 1, 2008, equipment that recovers and recycles HFC-134a refrigerant and equipment that recovers and recycles HFC-134a refrigerant and recharges systems with HFC-134a refrigerant must meet the standards set forth in Appendix C of this subpart based upon J2788

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.36, Approved refrigerant handling equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: HFC-134a, recover only: Appendix D (based on SAE J2810), effective October 31, 2008.
points.quote: Effective October 31, 2008, equipment that recovers but does not recycle HFC-134a refrigerant must meet the standards set forth in Appendix D of this subpart based upon J2810

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.36, Approved refrigerant handling equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: CFC-12 and HFC-134a recovered and recycled with common circuitry: Appendix E.
points.quote: Equipment that recovers and recycles both CFC-12 and HFC-134a using common circuitry must meet the standards set forth in appendix E of this subpart

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.36, Approved refrigerant handling equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Recover-only equipment for refrigerants other than CFC-12, HFC-134a and HFO-1234yf: Appendix F.
points.quote: Equipment that recovers but does not recycle refrigerants other than CFC-12, HFC-134a, and HFO-1234yf must meet the standards set forth in appendix F of this subpart

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.36, Approved refrigerant handling equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: HFO-1234yf, recover and recycle from MVACs and recharge MVAC systems: SAE J2843, incorporated by reference.
points.quote: Equipment that recovers and recycles HFO-1234yf refrigerant from MVACs and recharges MVAC systems with HFO-1234yf refrigerant must meet the standards set forth in SAE J2843 (incorporated by reference, see § 82.31).

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.36, Approved refrigerant handling equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Recover only (no recycling) for contaminated HFC-134a and/or HFO-1234yf from MVACs: SAE J2851, incorporated by reference.
points.quote: Equipment that recovers but does not recycle contaminated HFC-134a and/or HFO-1234yf refrigerant from MVACs must meet the standards set forth in SAE J2851 (incorporated by reference, see § 82.31).

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.36, Approved refrigerant handling equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Recover, recycle and recharge both HFO-1234yf and R-134a from MVACs: SAE J3030, incorporated by reference.
points.quote: Equipment that recovers, recycles, and recharges both HFO-1234yf and R-134a from MVACs must meet the standards set forth in SAE J3030 (incorporated by reference, see § 82.31).

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.36, Approved refrigerant handling equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

topics.notCovered: We do not set out the technical contents of SAE J2843, J2851 and J3030, because they are incorporated by reference and their text is not printed in Subpart B.

points.text: Refrigerant recycling equipment not certified under 82.36(a) is considered approved if it is substantially identical to the applicable certified equipment and meets the purchase-date condition for its type.
points.quote: Refrigerant recycling equipment that has not been certified under paragraph (a) of this section shall be considered approved if it is substantially identical to the applicable equipment certified under paragraph (a) of this section, and:

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.36, Approved refrigerant handling equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: CFC-12 recover-and-recycle equipment must have been initially purchased before September 4, 1991; CFC-12 recover-only equipment before April 22, 1992.
points.quote: For equipment that recovers and recycles CFC-12 refrigerant, it was initially purchased before September 4, 1991; (ii) For equipment that recovers but does not recycle CFC-12 refrigerant, it was initially purchased before April 22, 1992;

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.36, Approved refrigerant handling equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: HFC-134a recover-and-recycle and HFC-134a recover-only equipment must have been initially purchased before March 6, 1996.
points.quote: For equipment that recovers and recycles HFC-134a refrigerant, it was initially purchased before March 6, 1996; (iv) For equipment that recovers but does not recycle HFC-134a refrigerant, it was initially purchased before March 6, 1996;

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.36, Approved refrigerant handling equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Recover-only equipment for any single, specific refrigerant other than CFC-12 or HFC-134a, and equipment recycling HFC-134a and CFC-12 with common circuitry, must also have been initially purchased before March 6, 1996.
points.quote: For equipment that recovers but does not recycle any single, specific refrigerant other than CFC-12 or HFC-134a, it was initially purchased before March 6, 1996; and (vi) For equipment that recovers and recycles HFC-134a and CFC-12 refrigerant using common circuitry, it was initially purchased before March 6, 1996.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.36, Approved refrigerant handling equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Equipment manufacturers or owners may ask EPA to decide whether equipment is substantially identical by submitting an application and supporting documents.
points.quote: Equipment manufacturers or owners may request a determination by the Administrator by submitting an application and supporting documents that indicate that the equipment is substantially identical to approved equipment

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.36, Approved refrigerant handling equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Equipment that fails to meet the appropriate standards will not be considered approved.
points.quote: Equipment that fails to meet appropriate standards will not be considered approved.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.36, Approved refrigerant handling equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: CFC-12 recovery or recovery-and-recycling equipment that is neither certified nor approved as substantially identical is considered approved for MVAC-like appliances if it was made or imported before November 15, 1993 and can reduce system pressure to 102 mm of mercury vacuum under Appendix A conditions.
points.quote: Refrigerant recycling equipment that recovers or recovers and recycles CFC-12 refrigerant and has not been certified under paragraph (a) or approved under paragraphs(b)(1) and (b)(2) of this section shall be considered approved for use with an MVAC-like appliance if it was manufactured or imported before November 15, 1993, and is capable of reducing the system pressure to 102 mm of mercury vacuum under the conditions set forth in appendix A of this subpart.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.36, Approved refrigerant handling equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: EPA maintains a list of approved equipment by manufacturer and model; anyone wanting a copy sends a written inquiry to the address given in 82.36(b).
points.quote: The Administrator will maintain a list of approved equipment by manufacturer and model. Persons interested in obtaining a copy of the list should send written inquiries to the address in paragraph (b) of this section.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.36, Approved refrigerant handling equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)
